title: Google auth
content:
## Overview

Google authentication enables your Emergent app to let users sign in with their Google accounts. This integration uses OAuth 2.0 and requires credentials from the Google Cloud Console.

<Info>
Google auth is handled through Emergent's managed authentication system. Once configured, your app can request user profile data, email addresses, and optional scopes like Google Calendar or Drive access.
</Info>

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, ensure you have:

- A Google account with access to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com)
- An Emergent app where you want to enable Google sign-in
- Appropriate billing enabled in Google Cloud (required for OAuth consent screen configuration)

## Setting up Google OAuth credentials

<Steps>
<Step title="Create a Google Cloud project">
Navigate to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com) and create a new project or select an existing one. Give it a descriptive name that matches your Emergent app.
</Step>

<Step title="Enable the Google+ API">
In your Google Cloud project, go to **APIs & Services > Library**. Search for "Google+ API" and click **Enable**. This API is required for basic profile information access.
</Step>

<Step title="Configure the OAuth consent screen">
Go to **APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen**:

- Choose **External** for user type (unless you have a Google Workspace organization)
- Fill in the required fields:
  - App name
  - User support email
  - Developer contact email
- Add your app's logo (optional but recommended)
- Click **Save and Continue**

For scopes, add the basic Google profile scopes:
- `userinfo.email`
- `userinfo.profile`

<Tip>
If your app needs additional Google services (Calendar, Drive, etc.), add those scopes here. You'll need to submit your app for verification if requesting sensitive scopes.
</Tip>
</Step>

<Step title="Create OAuth 2.0 credentials">
Navigate to **APIs & Services > Credentials** and click **Create Credentials > OAuth 2.0 Client ID**.

Select **Web application** as the application type, then configure:

- **Name**: A descriptive identifier (e.g., "Emergent Production")
- **Authorized JavaScript origins**: Add your Emergent app's URL:
  ```
  https://your-app-name.emergent.build
  ```
- **Authorized redirect URIs**: Add the callback URL:
  ```
  https://your-app-name.emergent.build/api/auth/callback/google
  ```

<Warning>
The redirect URI must match exactly. Include both your production domain and any custom domains you've configured.
</Warning>

Click **Create** and save the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** that appear.
</Step>

<Step title="Add credentials to Emergent">
In the Emergent chat interface, tell the agent to configure Google authentication:

```
Add Google authentication using:
Client ID: YOUR_CLIENT_ID
Client Secret: YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET
```

The agent will securely store these credentials and configure your app's authentication routes.

<Note>
Credentials are encrypted at rest. You can update them anytime by providing new values through chat.
</Note>
</Step>

<Step title="Test the integration">
Ask the agent to add a sign-in button to your app, then preview the app and click **Sign in with Google**. You should be redirected to Google's consent screen, then back to your app upon successful authentication.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Accessing user data

Once a user authenticates, your app can access their Google profile information. The typical data available includes:

- Email address
- Full name
- Profile picture URL
- Google user ID

<CodeGroup>
```typescript Example: Accessing user session
// In your app code
const session = await getSession();
if (session?.user) {
  const { email, name, image } = session.user;
  console.log(`Signed in as ${name} (${email})`);
}
```

```python Example: Backend route
# Python backend accessing authenticated user
from emergent import get_current_user

@app.route('/profile')
def profile():
    user = get_current_user()
    return {
        'email': user.email,
        'name': user.name,
        'picture': user.picture
    }
```
</CodeGroup>

## Additional scopes

If your app needs access to Google services beyond basic profile data, request additional OAuth scopes.

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Common scopes">
| Scope | Access |
|-------|--------|
| `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly` | Read calendar events |
| `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` | Access files created by the app |
| `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send` | Send email on user's behalf |
| `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email` | Email address (included by default) |
| `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.profile` | Basic profile info (included by default) |
</Tab>

<Tab title="Requesting scopes">
Tell the agent which scopes your app needs:

```
Update Google auth to request calendar read access and Gmail send permissions
```

The agent will modify the OAuth configuration and prompt users to grant additional permissions on next sign-in.

<Warning>
Sensitive or restricted scopes require Google's app verification process, which can take several weeks. Plan accordingly if you need scopes like full Gmail access or Drive file modification.
</Warning>
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Multiple environments

When working with staging or development environments, add their redirect URIs to your Google Cloud OAuth client:

<Steps>
<Step title="Add development URLs">
In Google Cloud Console, edit your OAuth 2.0 client and add:

- `https://your-app-name-staging.emergent.build/api/auth/callback/google`
- `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google` (for local testing)
</Step>

<Step title="Use the same credentials">
You can reuse the same Client ID and Secret across environments, or create separate OAuth clients for better isolation and monitoring.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Error: redirect_uri_mismatch">
The callback URL in your Google Cloud Console doesn't match the one your app is using. Double-check that:

- The protocol is `https://` (not `http://`) for production
- The domain matches exactly, including subdomains
- The path is `/api/auth/callback/google`
- There are no trailing slashes or typos
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Users see 'This app isn't verified'">
This warning appears when requesting scopes beyond basic profile. Options:

1. Add test users in Google Cloud Console (up to 100) who won't see the warning
2. Submit your app for verification if you need public access
3. Users can click "Advanced > Go to [app name]" to proceed anyway

For internal apps, adding specific users as testers is usually sufficient.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Authentication works but user data is missing">
Ensure your app is requesting the correct scopes. The default scopes include email and basic profile. If you need additional data, explicitly request those scopes and have users re-authenticate to grant the new permissions.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I use Google auth with a custom domain?">
Yes. When you configure a custom domain for your Emergent app, add the custom domain's callback URL to your Google OAuth client's authorized redirect URIs:

```
https://yourdomain.com/api/auth/callback/google
```

See the [custom domain](/custom-domain) guide for more details.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Security considerations

<Callout type="warning" title="Keep credentials secure">
Never commit your Client Secret to version control or expose it in client-side code. Emergent stores these securely and only uses them server-side during the OAuth flow.
</Callout>

Best practices:

- **Rotate credentials** periodically, especially if you suspect exposure
- **Limit scopes** to only what your app genuinely needs
- **Monitor usage** in Google Cloud Console to detect unusual activity
- **Use different OAuth clients** for production and development environments when handling sensitive data
